propositions: rebar-implement skill Phase 4d dispatches a subagent without specifying a model tier, causing it to silently inherit the expensive orchestrator tier and eliminate cost savings
the skill lacks documented guidance on which work is safe to delegate to cheaper models and how to escalate when a cheaper implementer proves insufficient
existing held-out test validation (4e) and test authoring (4b) must remain strong-tier to preserve TDD guarantees, while implementation can use cheaper capabilities
Phase 3 and 4a dispatch logic need seam annotations distinguishing cheap-shaped work (research, discovery, grep) from strong-tier-required work (spec derivation)
a new escalation ladder (4e-bis) must distinguish routine held-out iteration from model-capability-driven escalation triggers
